candidates.name: Mycosis Fungoides
support_spans: perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula
exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium
lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7
monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated
candidates.why: The presence of atypical lymphocytes, perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates, and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement supports the diagnosis of Mycosis Fungoides.

candidates.name: Cutaneous T-cell Lymphoma
support_spans: erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with some papules
atypical lymphocytes
CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1
candidates.why: The clinical presentation and histopathologic findings, including the presence of atypical lymphocytes and an abnormal CD4 to CD8 ratio, are consistent with Cutaneous T-cell Lymphoma.

candidates.name: Folliculotropic Mycosis Fungoides
support_spans: perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula
focal mild follicular mucin deposition
lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD4
candidates.why: The specific involvement of the hair follicles, as evidenced by perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates and follicular mucin deposition, suggests Folliculotropic Mycosis Fungoides.
